sections.markdown:
## B — Audience, level and prerequisites: Class C privilege, application requirements, proof documents, insurance and collision duties
Audience: every first-time Oregon Class C applicant, especially applicants under eighteen, who face extra permit, practice and school requirements.
Why it matters to a first-timer: the teen permit period and practice hours decide when a license can be issued [A02], the insurance minimums are exact money amounts [A05], and collision report triggers use a damage threshold and a short deadline [A06].
Level: exact-number and list recall (ages, hours, document expiry windows, insurance minimums, report triggers); heavy load.
Prerequisites: the testing section, especially the knowledge, vision and drive tests and the Class C scope.

corpus_stability.reason: The Oregon Driver Manual is a two-year edition (the front cover names a two-year span and the back cover carries a single form revision code); fees and office details are sent to the DMV website rather than printed, and nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year.
